prompt.context_jp: 「彼らの背後には さらに大きな 敵____いるということに」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「彼らの背後には さらに大きな 敵____いるということに」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces this enemy as new information.

feedback.correct_en: Kiritani is revealing the existence of a bigger enemy for the first time — a classic 'new information / existence' context that takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 敵 as an already-known topic, which contradicts the surprise-reveal nuance of 気が付いた.

contrast_examples.en: There is a cat in the room. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 「彼ら____ ただ操られていたんですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「彼ら____ ただ操られていたんですよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks 彼ら as the known topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: 彼ら was already introduced; Kiritani is now commenting on them as the established topic, so は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a new-information identification ('it is they who were being manipulated'), not a comment on a known group.

contrast_examples.jp: 操られていたのは彼らがだ。

prompt.context_jp: 「この作品の良さ____ 分からないんですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「この作品の良さ____ 分からないんですか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the object of 分かる.

feedback.correct_en: 分かる takes が for the thing understood — a stative verb pattern, not an action on an object.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is used with action verbs; 分かる is stative and takes が for its complement.

prompt.context_jp: 「相手____夫です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「相手____夫です」
prompt.prompt_en: Fujiiwa answers who her date partner is.

feedback.correct_en: 相手 ('the partner [in question]') is the established topic from the preceding conversation about her date; は comments on it.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly re-introduce 相手 as new information — but it's already the thing being discussed.

contrast_examples.en: It's a colleague who is the partner. (focus on 同僚)

prompt.context_jp: 「夫____私の仕事を理解しています」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「夫____私の仕事を理解しています」
prompt.prompt_en: Fujiiwa explains about her husband.

feedback.correct_en: Her husband was just mentioned; she is making a comment about him as the topic — 'as for my husband, he understands.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like an identification ('it is my husband who understands'), which doesn't fit this reassuring statement.

contrast_examples.en: It's my husband who is at fault. (focus)

prompt.context_jp: 「お前の力____必要なんだ⇒ なっ 頼む！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「お前の力____必要なんだ」
prompt.prompt_en: Kaizuka pleads: it's YOUR help he needs.

feedback.correct_en: Adjectives like 必要 take が for what is needed. The emphasis also fits exhaustive-listing が — 'it is your help that I need.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would downgrade the urgency and sound like a casual topic comment, losing Kaizuka's begging tone.

prompt.context_jp: 「これ____少なくとも 3日はかかる分量です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「これ____少なくとも 3日はかかる分量です」
prompt.prompt_en: Fujiiwa points out this manuscript's volume.

feedback.correct_en: これ refers to the manuscript already in front of them — an established topic Fujiiwa is characterizing. は fits naturally.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify これ as new info, but the manuscript is clearly the ongoing topic of discussion.

contrast_examples.en: This is difficult. (comment on known thing)

prompt.context_jp: 「校閲のミス____ 会社全体のミスになるんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「校閲のミス____ 会社全体のミスになるんです」
prompt.prompt_en: Fujiiwa makes a general statement about proofreading mistakes.

feedback.correct_en: This is a generic statement defining what a proofreading mistake IS. Generic/definitional statements take は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would point to one specific mistake as new info, but Fujiiwa is stating a general principle.

prompt.context_jp: 部屋の中____薄暗く、返事____なかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋の中は薄暗く、返事____なかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 返事 in this negative-existence clause.

feedback.correct_en: Negative existence of an expected thing frequently uses は — 'as for a response, there wasn't one.' It conveys contrast with the expected reply.
feedback.incorrect_en: が is grammatical but neutral; は better matches the narrative emphasis on the absence of the expected answer.

contrast_examples.en: There was no response (as expected to be).

prompt.context_jp: 「あのさ 私____ずっと… 無理してたんだ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私____ずっと… 無理してたんだ」
prompt.prompt_en: Yukito begins a confession about himself.

feedback.correct_en: Yukito is making 私 the topic and commenting on his own long-standing state — classic topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify 'it was I who...' as if contrasting with someone else; the context is simple self-reflection.

prompt.context_jp: 藤岩のさりげない一言____、部内の空気を数秒だけ凍りつかせた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 藤岩のさりげない一言____、部内の空気を数秒だけ凍りつかせた。
prompt.prompt_en: The narrator introduces Fujiiwa's remark as the cause.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence introduces a new narrative element (Fujiiwa's remark) as the agent causing the atmosphere to freeze — new info が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the remark as a known topic, but it's just being introduced into the scene as the surprising trigger.

contrast_examples.en: A single remark changed the atmosphere.

contrast_examples.jp: その一言は印象的だった。

prompt.context_jp: 時間との勝負を前に、貝塚の額に____汗が浮かんでいる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 貝塚の額には汗____浮かんでいる。
prompt.prompt_en: Narrative: sweat appears on Kaizuka's forehead.

feedback.correct_en: Sweat is being introduced into the scene as a new, visible detail — descriptive new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark sweat as a prior topic, but the narrator is just now pointing it out to the reader.

prompt.context_jp: 隣席の藤岩____だけは、いつも通り黙々と朱字を入れ続けている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 隣席の藤岩だけ____、いつも通り黙々と朱字を入れ続けている。
prompt.prompt_en: Everyone else is excited; only Fujiiwa is working silently.

feedback.correct_en: だけは adds contrastive emphasis — Fujiiwa, in contrast to the buzzing colleagues, keeps working. This is textbook contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が wouldn't carry the contrastive 'only she, unlike the others' nuance that defines this sentence.

prompt.context_jp: 数字____残酷なほど正直で、編集者が幾ら庇っても隠しきれない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 数字____残酷なほど正直で...
prompt.prompt_en: Narration: a generic truth about numbers.

feedback.correct_en: A generic, proverb-like statement about numbers in general. Generic statements take は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would point at a specific set of numbers as new info, but the narrator is stating a universal truth.

prompt.context_jp: 部長が貝塚に:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「決定事項を____な」
prompt.prompt_en: The director forbids Kaizuka from reopening a closed matter.

feedback.correct_en: 蒸し返す literally 're-steam,' idiomatically means to bring up an already-settled issue again — exactly what the director accuses Kaizuka of.
feedback.incorrect_en: 持ち上げる means to lift/flatter, and 引き下げる means to withdraw — neither fits 'rehashing a decided matter.'

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が藤岩に頼む場面:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ムチャなことを言ってるのは ____承知です」
prompt.prompt_en: Kaizuka admits he's asking something unreasonable.

feedback.correct_en: 重々承知 is a set polite business phrase meaning 'I'm fully/keenly aware.' It's the standard collocation here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 重たく doesn't collocate with 承知; 大変 would sound awkward and non-idiomatic in this fixed expression.

contrast_examples.jp: ご無理は重々承知しております。
contrast_examples.en: I'm fully aware this is a lot to ask.

prompt.context_jp: 藤岩が悦子に香水を少しもらう時:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「____なければ 私にも ひと吹き お願いします」
prompt.prompt_en: Fujiiwa politely asks for a spritz if it's not a problem.

feedback.correct_en: 差し支えなければ ('if it's no trouble') is a standard polite hedge, fitting Fujiiwa's formal register.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気にしなければ changes the meaning to 'if you don't mind it' (focused on feeling), and 問題ありなければ is ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.jp: 差し支えなければ名前を教えてください。
contrast_examples.en: If it's no trouble, please tell me your name.
Please, if you'd like. (similar polite hedge)

prompt.context_jp: 悦子が徹夜依頼を断ろうとする場面:
prompt.prompt_jp: それでも悦子の口から出た答えは、彼女なりの____の抵抗であった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word describing Etsuko's best effort at resistance.

feedback.correct_en: 精一杯 means 'to the utmost of one's ability.' Combined with 彼女なりの, it conveys that her weak excuse was all she could manage.
feedback.incorrect_en: 真っ最中 means 'in the middle of,' and 一方通行 means 'one-way' — neither fits the idea of 'maximum effort.'

contrast_examples.jp: 今、作業の真っ最中です。
contrast_examples.en: I'm right in the middle of work.

prompt.context_jp: 普段は口の悪い貝塚が丁寧になる様子:
prompt.prompt_jp: 普段は口の悪い編集者が別人のように腰を____いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that forms the idiom for 'behaving humbly.'

feedback.correct_en: 腰を低くする is the fixed idiom meaning 'to lower one's posture / act humbly/deferentially.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 腰を下げる means literally lowering the hips (sitting down); 腰を丸める means slouching — neither matches 'acting humbly.'

contrast_examples.jp: 腰を低くしてお願いする。

prompt.context_jp: 校閲作業の積み重ねを表す諺:
prompt.prompt_jp: ____と言う通り、一文字一文字の確認が、いつしか本一冊を支える骨組みになっている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the proverb about small efforts accumulating.

choices.text: 塵も積もれば山となる

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる ('even dust piles up into a mountain') perfectly matches the idea that each small character-check builds the whole book.
feedback.incorrect_en: 猿も木から落ちる is about even experts making mistakes; 石の上にも三年 is about perseverance over time — different nuances.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が幸人に:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「編集者と作家は ____なんだよ！」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom Kaizuka uses for editor-writer relationship.

feedback.correct_en: 二人三脚 (three-legged race) is used metaphorically for two people working closely together — perfect for a writer/editor team.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一石二鳥 means 'two birds with one stone,' and 一期一会 is 'once-in-a-lifetime encounter' — neither describes cooperation.

contrast_examples.jp: 夫婦二人三脚で店を開いた。
contrast_examples.en: The couple opened the shop working together.

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が校閲部に戻ってくる場面:
prompt.prompt_jp: 貝塚が肩を____て駆け込んできた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that forms the idiom for 'with tense/angry shoulders.'

feedback.correct_en: 肩を怒らせる means to square/tense one's shoulders in anger — matching Kaizuka's frustration after being refused.
feedback.incorrect_en: 肩を落とす expresses dejection/disappointment, and 肩をすくめる means shrugging — the wrong emotional register.

prompt.context_jp: 藤岩の電話を聞いた後の描写:
prompt.prompt_jp: 藤岩が最後に発した一言だけが、妙に長く____に残った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for where the line lingered.

feedback.correct_en: 耳に残る is the standard collocation for 'words lingering/echoing in one's ears' after being heard.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心に残る ('stays in the heart') fits emotional memories, and 頭に残る is less idiomatic. 耳に残る specifically evokes the sound/voice replaying.

contrast_examples.en: That song stays in my ears.
The kindness stays in my heart.

prompt.context_jp: 藤岩が夫に電話で徹夜を伝える場面。どちらが自然ですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits Fujiiwa's polite, composed tone when telling her husband?

choices.text: 今夜 どうしても やらなければ ならない仕事が入りまして
今夜 絶対にやる仕事が来ちゃって

feedback.correct_en: Fujiiwa consistently speaks in formal, careful register even to her husband; やらなければならない仕事が入りまして fits her characterization.
feedback.incorrect_en: やる仕事が来ちゃって is casual and childish-sounding, clashing with Fujiiwa's deliberate, polite personality.

prompt.context_jp: 悦子の言い訳に貝塚が苛立つ場面。どちらが貝塚らしい？
prompt.prompt_en: Which line fits Kaizuka's blunt, frustrated outburst?

choices.text: んなわけねぇだろ！ 面倒くせぇな！
そのようなわけはないでしょう。面倒ですね。

feedback.correct_en: Kaizuka is a rough, blunt editor; the contracted ねぇ and 面倒くせぇ match his gruff speech style here.
feedback.incorrect_en: The polite version sounds like a different person entirely — Kaizuka would never speak this way when frustrated.

contrast_examples.jp: 冗談はおやめください。

prompt.context_jp: 藤岩がゲラ作成を申し出る場面。どちらが自然ですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'so we can have more time'?

choices.text: 少しでも長く 校閲の時間を取ることができます
少しだけ長く 校閲の時間を持つことが可能です

feedback.correct_en: 時間を取る is the natural collocation for 'secure time,' and 少しでも長く ('even a bit longer') fits the urgent tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 時間を持つ is unnatural in Japanese (it's a direct translation of English 'have time'), and 可能です sounds stiffer than needed.

contrast_examples.jp: 少しでも長く残りたい。
contrast_examples.en: Want to stay even a bit longer.

prompt.context_jp: 貝塚が校閲部員に粘りたいと謝る場面。どちらが自然？
prompt.prompt_en: Which apology-request sounds more natural in a professional setting?

choices.text: 皆さんには 申し訳ないんですけども 納得するまで ここは 粘りたいんです
皆さんに 悪いですが 納得するまで ここで 粘りたいです

feedback.correct_en: 申し訳ない is the standard professional apology; けども softens the request, and には highlights the people being inconvenienced. Natural workplace phrasing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 悪いですが is casual/blunt among peers; combined with 粘りたいです (no softener) it sounds abrupt and less professional.

contrast_examples.jp: 申し訳ないんですが、もう少し時間を…
contrast_examples.en: I'm terribly sorry, but a bit more time...

contrast_examples.jp: 悪いけど、もうちょっと。

prompt.context_jp: 幸人が悦子に告白する場面。どちらが自然？
prompt.prompt_en: Which casual confession fits the scene between Yukito and Etsuko?

choices.text: 今更だけど 俺 えっちゃんのことが 好きだよ
今更ですが 僕は えっちゃんを 愛しております

feedback.correct_en: Yukito and Etsuko are close friends; the casual 俺/だよ and 〜のことが好き is the natural Japanese confession register.
feedback.incorrect_en: 愛しております is overly formal/literary and 僕 clashes with Yukito's established casual 俺. It sounds like a stiff translation, not a confession.
